questions.coherence: One design. The witness again has one owned termination path. On Windows the verdict now comes from the observed exit, bounded by the lifecycle that ADR-0189 already documents, and non-Windows close then kill is unchanged. remaining() feeds the helper's spawn timeout from the same coordinator, so the 2 s helper timeout and the 2 s reserve no longer cut each other off. The harness side shares one product-tree notion (same-tree.mjs) between check-ci-evidence and last-ci, and one mark rule (endsWith) between land, check-checkpoint and last-ci. Two seams remain. last-ci's Fixes-ci match is still keyed to a run id while its INTERMITTENT check is keyed to a tree, so a real fix in flight reads as an unclaimed red (F2). The same-tree reading is bounded by a 30-run page that the tree concept does not respect (F1).

That is the correct path. The gaps follow. (1) M18.196's same-tree check reads only `actions/runs?branch=main&event=push&per_page=30` (gh: --limit 30), across ci, gates and release. That is about 10 ci runs, while a product tree in this milestone routinely spans 9 or more pushes. The diagnosis places the failures in heavy runs (verify of 1207 s or more), and the new bound is the lifecycle end, up to about 118 s per session. The 129-member case uses two sessions in sequence. findings.failure_scenario: On loaded Windows runners closes routinely take 10-60 s. The three closing greens look clean, and M18.195 closes. Windows verify then grows toward its 25-minute step, the step times out with no failing test, and the next agent writes another envelope ADR (the ADR-0191/0197/0209 pattern) without knowing the witness close is where the time goes. A Windows user's 129-member import also pauses for minutes, with nothing in any log saying why.
findings.recommendation: Print an 'exited-after-reserve' WITNESS_CLEANUP line with the wait on a slow success, and let the pack-import e2e print those lines on success too. M18.195 still closes on its own criterion. This row follows.
